decision: KEEP Node/ECMAScript build tooling; FIX distribution lifecycle with one shell-free stage wrapper and failure cleanup, plus noEmitOnError.
constraints: Linux/Windows Node SDK package builds must invalidate prior output before contract checking and withdraw partial output on handled stage failures.
Retain existing versioned generator and AJV standalone output, pinned TypeScript, explicit npm pack allowlist, offline execution and source boundaries.
No full clone, container, privileged installation or new runtime dependency. Child stages run sequentially with a 30000 ms timeout each; one writer per package directory.

alternatives.technology: Node ECMAScript wrapper using child_process and fs
alternatives.assessment: Selected: launch the current Node executable with fixed argument arrays and absolute working directory; avoids shell quoting and platform-specific tsc shims. A single failure boundary owns generated dist cleanup and leaves source untouched. Executable regressions reproduce stale output before the correction and verify recovery bytes.

Rejected: the observed && chain stopped after failure but retained prior or partially emitted output. Reliable cleanup traps and process invocation would require platform-specific shell handling across Windows and Linux.

Credible timeout and cleanup primitives, but this independently usable Node package would gain a Python runtime requirement without eliminating any Node compiler stage. No Python build-host contract is required by this package.

Credible typed native process handling, but a binary per host platform still launches Node and needs explicit cleanup logic. This small build-only sequential workflow has no native throughput requirement; no measured correctness or deployment benefit justifies migration.

limits: A successful build is not a signed release, customer installation or real-time qualification. Only the generated dist directory is owned by the wrapper.

Handled failures withdraw output when the filesystem permits cleanup. Parent termination, power loss, concurrent writers and hostile filesystem changes are outside this check; consumers must still require successful build/package gates.
Direct validator invocation removes only its validators.cjs output after dependencies load. Whole-package build also clears dist before launching any dependency-bearing stage.
No alternative runtime performance benchmark or browser/Windows local acceptance is claimed. Stages have requested process timeouts, not real-time guarantees.
